what_is_wrong: Duplicate cannot create a new dated version of a tax head under the same tax name, because tax_heads carries UNIQUE KEY ux_tax_heads_scope_name (scope, tax_name) with no date component. This makes the endpoint's own documented purpose unreachable, and it is a closed loop: once a head has been used, PUT rejects any arithmetic edit with a message that explicitly says 'use Duplicate instead' â€” and Duplicate then rejects the same-named new version. The only escape is renaming the tax (e.g. 'ZZTest PT Fixed (v2)'), which changes the head's identity and the label shown on documents. The engine is built for the multi-version model the constraint forbids: tax_engine.select_effective_head(snapshots, as_of) picks the snapshot in force on a date from a LIST of same-identity heads, and payroll_runs.py calls _in_force_heads(...) to filter heads by scope + date.

status_observed: 200 with a computed amount for a head that is not in force on the requested date
what_is_wrong: TaxCalculationRequest declares an `as_of` date field, but the handler never reads body.as_of. The head is loaded by id and calculated unconditionally, so a caller asking 'what is this tax on this date' gets a figure from a head whose applies_from/applies_until range does not contain that date. app/services/tax_head_lookup.py:66-67 already contains the exact guard that should fire ('Tax head ... is not in force on ...'), and it is never called from this route. A silently ignored date parameter on a tax calculator is a wrong number, not a missing feature.
